title: Sync extension manifest
description: What a package says about itself. Four things read this file — the packer, the registry's CI, Sync's Rust loader and the window — and this is what validates it for all of them. Sync's reader is the authority: where the two disagree, the reader is right and this is behind.

manifestVersion.description: The format this file is written in. Read before anything else, so a package from the future is told it needs a newer Sync rather than being told a field name is unknown — which would be true and useless.

id.description: Permanent, and the namespace every kind it publishes is prefixed with. Nothing that could be a path: an id with a slash in it escapes the artefact directory.

version.description: The package's own version, which is neither the API's nor the application's.

summary.description: One line, in the catalogue's voice: what a project gains by adding it.

description.description: What it is, at the length a decision to install one deserves.

icon.description: A name from the shared icon library, resolved by the host at load. A name the host cannot draw is shown neutrally rather than guessed at.

syncApi.description: A semver range over the host's SYNC_API_VERSION, such as ^2.0. Checked before a line of the package is executed.

capabilities.description: Named things the build must be able to do. A capability the host has never heard of is a refusal, not a warning: it arrives in exactly one situation — a package built against a newer host — and treating it as satisfied would run an extension that asked for something and did not get it.

requires.description: What it needs from the project rather than from the build.

areas.description: The sections it contributes to the window. An extension is not necessarily a screen, and declaring none is an ordinary answer.

id.description: Unique within the extension. The window addresses it as <extension>/<id>.

description.description: What the section is for, where a column needs explaining.

frame.description: One of the shapes the shell draws, and the module must fill exactly that frame's columns: browse has a navigator and an inspector, list a navigator, detail an inspector, single neither. Returning a column the frame does not have fails to install rather than being dropped.

badge.description: A count the host draws on this section's row. Nothing of the package runs to produce it, which is the point: a section is mounted the first time it is visited, so a number only a mounted section could raise would be missing on the first launch after a project is opened — exactly when somebody wants it. Omit it for a section with nothing to count.

kinds.description: Which kinds are counted, and omitting it counts every kind this section opens — the ordinary answer, because the manifest has already said which those are. Name them only where one extension has two sections over one vocabulary. Each is prefixed with the extension id, by the rule opens.kinds reads: a badge over another extension's records is a number nobody can act on.

freshness.description: Which of the states the engine derives are counted, and omitting it counts every state.

types.description: Paths inside the package, each one type definition. Every kind they publish is prefixed with the extension's id and a dot: two extensions may both want to call something a decision, and neither may redefine the other's.

opens.description: Which records this extension knows how to show. Publishing a type and opening one are two contributions, not one.

kinds.description: Kinds it opens, which are normally the kinds it publishes. A kind belonging to another extension is refused.

projectTypes.description: Whether it opens the types the project made itself. Exactly one installed extension should claim it; the host prefers whichever the project declares.

prompt.description: Path to what a connected agent is told, as prose. Written into the project on install, because the agent reads it through a server that has never seen the catalogue.

dependencies.description: What it needs fetched before it works well.

npm.description: Packages from npm, by name. What the host fetches is the adapter set it knows how to fetch — installing an arbitrary package on an extension's say-so is a much larger permission than the one being asked for.

ui.description: The built ES module, relative to the package root. Optional, because an extension that publishes only a vocabulary and a prompt has no code to run — and required the moment it declares a section, because a section is drawn by code.

styles.description: The built stylesheet, relative to the package root. The host adds it to the document when it loads the module and takes it away with it. Optional, and only meaningful beside `ui`: it holds the utility rules this package's own markup uses, which the window's stylesheet does not contain — Tailwind generates only what it finds in the window's own source, and a package is not in it. It carries no values: every colour and step in it is a `var()` the window defines, so retinting the window retints the package.

allOf.$comment: A section with nothing to draw it is refused rather than shipped as an empty column.
A stylesheet with no module to style is a file nobody asked for: styles are the markup's, and the markup is in the module.

insidePath.description: A path that stays inside the package: relative, no backslashes, no segment that is empty, `.` or `..`. A path that climbs reads a file the archive does not contain.
